title: Work Your Way In
aim: Move from the baseline to the kitchen line in small, balanced steps, and send hard balls back soft instead of popping them up (hitting them high enough to be attacked).

stages.title: One Step at a Time
stages.inShort: A feeds calm balls, and B steps in from the baseline one good drop at a time.
rules: A stands at the kitchen line and starts every ball: calm balls at B's feet.
B starts behind the baseline and plays a drop: a soft ball that lands in or near the kitchen.
Good drop: B takes one step forward and split-steps (a small hop that lands just as A hits). Step by step to the kitchen line, then back out to the baseline the same way.
Bad or high ball: B holds or steps back, and plays the next one soft.
Keep the stroke small: a little push and lift, not a big swing.
stages.tooEasy: A plays with pace at B's feet, so B has to decide under pressure whether to step in or hold.
stages.tooHard: A feeds only calm, easy balls, and B thinks only about the timing of the split-step.
stages.goodLooksLike: Balanced at every step, the soft ball stays low, and B only moves forward after a good ball.

stages.title: Survive the Pressure
stages.inShort: A attacks at the feet, and B resets soft from further and further back.
rules: A stands at the kitchen line and attacks with pace at B's feet. Every ball must stay in the court.
B plays resets: soft balls that take the pace off and land in front of A's feet, near the middle.
B moves to every ball but holds the set distance: first at the kitchen line, then about 1 m behind it, then about 2 m behind it.
High ball: B stays balanced and lowers the paddle, the ball will come down. A ball clearly flying out: let it go.
Points to 5: B only has to survive, A plays to win. Then swap roles.
stages.tooEasy: A plays at full pace, and only resets that land in the middle count for B.
stages.tooHard: A aims clearly at the feet and plays at moderate pace, so B can read every ball.
stages.goodLooksLike: Quiet feet, a loose grip, and resets that drop low in front of A instead of popping up.

stages.title: Seven Against Eleven
stages.inShort: B works in from the baseline on half the court, and A tries to keep B back.
rules: Half the court, lengthwise. A starts at the kitchen line, B behind the baseline.
No serve: A starts every rally with an easy ball to B. A start ball that is too hard or goes wrong is played again.
B works in with drops and resets. A keeps B back with soft volleys at the feet, no hard hits.
Once B reaches the kitchen line, anything goes: play the point out. Lobs are allowed.
Both score on every rally. A needs 11, B only 7, because B's job is harder. Then swap roles.
stages.tooEasy: A may now use every shot, hard hits included.
stages.tooHard: B may drive the first ball instead of dropping it, and A has to block it soft or step back.
stages.goodLooksLike: B moves forward only behind a low ball, split-steps as A hits, and holds or steps back after a high one.
